answer: One robust Sybil defense is a shared kernel of slashable stake escrow: every agent that wants transaction capacity locks tokens in a lagoon of staked capital for a fixed epoch. The network allocates throughput proportionally to stake, so a Sybil operator who splits one deposit across many fake identities gains no extra share - each island of identity divides, not multiplies, influence. Attack cost becomes linear: forging K identities needs K times the minimum escrow, while honest agents pool delegation cheaply, making each marginal Sybil identity expensive and useless.
